metadata.title: Encorafenib and Binimetinib Therapy
metadata.indication: Adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a confirmed BRAF V600 mutation.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.scope_note: Current catalogue-linked PDF retained and audited. Component pathways, recovery and source uncertainties are explicit. Independent clinical and oncology pharmacy review pending.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or the specialist authority specified in the current NCCP source.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Discuss every modification with the consultant and oncology pharmacy. Review current component doses, event history and recovery; no automatic numeric restart dose is calculated. Unentered domains remain unassessed.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding derived from NCCP 00563 Version 3. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.

source_conflicts.resolution: Table 2 prints 225g once daily; this is unsafe to operationalise. Do not silently change to 225 mg or retain the prior v3 200 mg. Pharmacy/source confirmation is required before a second reduction.

Opening treatment prose says both medicines once daily, but the actual treatment table and 12-hour instruction specify binimetinib 45 mg twice daily. Use the explicit table and retain this discrepancy.

Table 3 permits Grade 2 recovery/reduced restart after up to 4 weeks; p10 says permanently discontinue confirmed treatment-related ILD. Maintain hold and require documented clinical/pharmacy reconciliation before restart.
The printed Grade 3 liver row requires AST/ALT >5 AND bilirubin >2 ×ULN. Values >5–≤20 with bilirubin ≤2 have no exact row; flag review rather than invent a dose or imply clearance.

indications.description: Adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a confirmed BRAF V600 mutation.

treatment.schedule_summary: Encorafenib 450 mg once daily plus binimetinib 45 mg twice daily, 12 hours apart, continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The 28-day review convention is not a treatment break.
treatment.cycle_convention_note: Continuous daily oral treatment. 28 days is an administrative assessment convention, not a drug-free interval.

components.note: 12 hours apart; treatment table overrides opening once-daily prose.

treatment.administration: Normally swallow whole with water, with or without food; avoid grapefruit juice. Pharmacy-confirmed swallowing alternatives: Braftovi capsules may be opened in approximately 20 mL apple sauce and taken immediately; Mektovi 15 mg tablets may be dispersed in approximately 10 mL water/orange/apple juice, taken immediately, then rinse with approximately 10 mL and drink. Do not infer dispersion for the 45 mg tablet. Missed encorafenib: take only if >12 hours to next dose. Missed binimetinib: do not take if <6 hours to next dose. Do not replace either dose after vomiting.
treatment.dose_reduction_reference: Starting encorafenib 450 mg daily / binimetinib 45 mg twice daily; first reduction 300 mg /30 mg twice daily. The printed encorafenib second-reduction unit is erroneous and requires clarification; no automatic numeric second reduction. Limited encorafenib 100 mg data; stop if intolerant of 100 mg or binimetinib 30 mg twice daily.

action.message: Known component/excipient hypersensitivity is an NCCP exclusion.

rules.explanation: Known component/excipient hypersensitivity is an NCCP exclusion.

action.message: Pregnancy is an NCCP exclusion; seek urgent specialist advice for exposure.

rules.explanation: Pregnancy is an NCCP exclusion; seek urgent specialist advice for exposure.

action.message: Breastfeeding is an NCCP exclusion.

rules.explanation: Breastfeeding is an NCCP exclusion.

action.message: A validated BRAF V600 mutation is required.

rules.explanation: A validated BRAF V600 mutation is required.

action.message: ECOG 0–1 is the source eligibility range; ECOG 2–4 requires individual consultant review.

rules.explanation: ECOG 0–1 is the source eligibility range; ECOG 2–4 requires individual consultant review.

action.message: Confirm baseline and ongoing laboratory, heart, skin and other required surveillance before prescribing.

rules.explanation: Confirm baseline and ongoing laboratory, heart, skin and other required surveillance before prescribing.

action.message: Confirm each current dose, previous reductions and the exact interrupted event before any restart or reduction.

rules.explanation: Confirm each current dose, previous reductions and the exact interrupted event before any restart or reduction.

action.message: Check the current SmPC and interaction database, including hormonal contraception and all prescribed/nonprescribed medicines.

rules.explanation: Check the current SmPC and interaction database, including hormonal contraception and all prescribed/nonprescribed medicines.

action.message: Arrange prompt ophthalmic assessment and identify uveitis, RPED or RVO. New symptoms alone do not establish a diagnosis or a universal two-drug interruption rule.

rules.explanation: Arrange prompt ophthalmic assessment and identify uveitis, RPED or RVO. New symptoms alone do not establish a diagnosis or a universal two-drug interruption rule.

action.message: Prompt dermatology assessment/excision and pathology. Cutaneous SCC or a new primary melanoma does not by itself require a dose reduction in this source.

rules.explanation: Prompt dermatology assessment/excision and pathology. Cutaneous SCC or a new primary melanoma does not by itself require a dose reduction in this source.

action.message: Discuss benefit and risk for RAS-mutated non-cutaneous malignancy. Consider permanent encorafenib discontinuation for a new RAS-positive malignancy; this requires consultant judgment and linked binimetinib review.

rules.explanation: Discuss benefit and risk for RAS-mutated non-cutaneous malignancy. Consider permanent encorafenib discontinuation for a new RAS-positive malignancy; this requires consultant judgment and linked binimetinib review.

action.message: LVEF requires the institutional LLN, baseline, symptoms and grade. Do not infer an on-treatment hold from a universal 50% cutoff.

rules.explanation: LVEF requires the institutional LLN, baseline, symptoms and grade. Do not infer an on-treatment hold from a universal 50% cutoff.

action.message: Restart remains a consultant/pharmacy decision: confirm the event, peak/current grade, recovery, time since hold, recurrence and actual component doses. A resolved symptom alone is not overall clearance.

rules.explanation: Restart remains a consultant/pharmacy decision: confirm the event, peak/current grade, recovery, time since hold, recurrence and actual component doses. A resolved symptom alone is not overall clearance.

action.message: Any prior BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy is listed as an exclusion; this differs from 00415 advanced treatment failure.

rules.explanation: Any prior BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy is listed as an exclusion; this differs from 00415 advanced treatment failure.

action.message: Impaired cardiovascular function or significant cardiovascular disease is an exclusion.

rules.explanation: Impaired cardiovascular function or significant cardiovascular disease is an exclusion.

action.message: Impaired gastrointestinal function is an exclusion; resolve oral absorption and treatment suitability.

rules.explanation: Impaired gastrointestinal function is an exclusion; resolve oral absorption and treatment suitability.

action.message: Safety is not established with baseline LVEF below 50% or below institutional LLN. This baseline caution is distinct from the on-treatment >10-point decline pathway.

rules.explanation: Safety is not established with baseline LVEF below 50% or below institutional LLN. This baseline caution is distinct from the on-treatment >10-point decline pathway.

action.message: No renal dose adjustment is needed for encorafenib at CrCl ≥30 mL/min, or for binimetinib. Hepatic impairment and other dose restrictions remain separate.

rules.explanation: No renal dose adjustment is needed for encorafenib at CrCl ≥30 mL/min, or for binimetinib. Hepatic impairment and other dose restrictions remain separate.

action.message: At CrCl <30 mL/min or haemodialysis WITHOUT hepatic impairment, no encorafenib adjustment is expected; binimetinib also needs no renal adjustment. Preserve clinical monitoring and other reductions.

rules.explanation: At CrCl <30 mL/min or haemodialysis WITHOUT hepatic impairment, no encorafenib adjustment is expected; binimetinib also needs no renal adjustment. Preserve clinical monitoring and other reductions.

action.message: The severe-renal/dialysis encorafenib row applies only without hepatic impairment. Establish hepatic status and obtain specialist dosing advice for combined impairment; no automatic extrapolation.

rules.explanation: The severe-renal/dialysis encorafenib row applies only without hepatic impairment. Establish hepatic status and obtain specialist dosing advice for combined impairment; no automatic extrapolation.

action.message: Encorafenib: 67% of ORIGINAL dose, stated as 300 mg once daily, for Child-Pugh A. Confirm the starting/current dose and closer clinical/LFT/ECG monitoring; do not multiply reductions or increase a lower dose.

rules.explanation: Encorafenib: 67% of ORIGINAL dose, stated as 300 mg once daily, for Child-Pugh A. Confirm the starting/current dose and closer clinical/LFT/ECG monitoring; do not multiply reductions or increase a lower dose.

action.message: Encorafenib is NOT RECOMMENDED in Child-Pugh B/C. Do not treat this combination as eligible simply because the separate binimetinib row gives 30 mg twice daily for moderate/severe hepatic impairment.

rules.explanation: Encorafenib is NOT RECOMMENDED in Child-Pugh B/C. Do not treat this combination as eligible simply because the separate binimetinib row gives 30 mg twice daily for moderate/severe hepatic impairment.

action.message: Binimetinib: 67% of ORIGINAL dose, stated as 30 mg twice daily, for moderate/severe hepatic impairment. Reconcile encorafenib Child-Pugh status first; B/C is not recommended for encorafenib.

rules.explanation: Binimetinib: 67% of ORIGINAL dose, stated as 30 mg twice daily, for moderate/severe hepatic impairment. Reconcile encorafenib Child-Pugh status first; B/C is not recommended for encorafenib.

action.message: Establish the component-specific hepatic classification before selecting a dose; laboratory adverse-event grades are not interchangeable with Child-Pugh class.

rules.explanation: Establish the component-specific hepatic classification before selecting a dose; laboratory adverse-event grades are not interchangeable with Child-Pugh class.

action.message: Correct magnesium, potassium and other electrolyte abnormalities and control QT risk before and during treatment; integrate actual QTcF and cardiac assessment.

rules.explanation: Correct magnesium, potassium and other electrolyte abnormalities and control QT risk before and during treatment; integrate actual QTcF and cardiac assessment.

action.message: Interrupt binimetinib until severe hypertension is controlled using standard therapy.

rules.explanation: Interrupt binimetinib until severe hypertension is controlled using standard therapy.

action.message: While binimetinib is interrupted, the source reduces encorafenib from 450 to 300 mg daily. Confirm actual dose and prior reductions; never automatically increase an already lower dose. Permanent binimetinib discontinuation also discontinues encorafenib.

rules.explanation: While binimetinib is interrupted, the source reduces encorafenib from 450 to 300 mg daily. Confirm actual dose and prior reductions; never automatically increase an already lower dose. Permanent binimetinib discontinuation also discontinues encorafenib.

action.message: Binimetinib is not recommended with a history of RVO; resolve treatment suitability and the combination plan with the consultant.

rules.explanation: Binimetinib is not recommended with a history of RVO; resolve treatment suitability and the combination plan with the consultant.

action.message: Use binimetinib with caution for RVO risk factors; optimise modifiable risks and arrange ocular monitoring.

rules.explanation: Use binimetinib with caution for RVO risk factors; optimise modifiable risks and arrange ocular monitoring.

action.message: Review tumour lysis risk, monitor closely, treat promptly and consider prophylactic hydration. The regimen does not prescribe a universal hydration volume or urate-lowering dose.

rules.explanation: Review tumour lysis risk, monitor closely, treat promptly and consider prophylactic hydration. The regimen does not prescribe a universal hydration volume or urate-lowering dose.

action.message: Initially maintain both medicines for Grade 2 cutaneous reactions with supportive treatment. Worsening or failure to improve within 2 weeks changes the pathway.

rules.explanation: Initially maintain both medicines for Grade 2 cutaneous reactions with supportive treatment. Worsening or failure to improve within 2 weeks changes the pathway.

action.message: Hold both medicines until Grade 0–1. First Grade 2: same-dose restart; recurrent Grade 2: reduce binimetinib, while the encorafenib row says same dose. Verify history before prescribing.

rules.explanation: Hold both medicines until Grade 0–1. First Grade 2: same-dose restart; recurrent Grade 2: reduce binimetinib, while the encorafenib row says same dose. Verify history before prescribing.

action.message: Hold both medicines until Grade 0–1. Resume same dose for first occurrence or reduced dose for recurrent Grade 3, after consultant/pharmacy verification.

rules.explanation: Hold both medicines until Grade 0–1. Resume same dose for first occurrence or reduced dose for recurrent Grade 3, after consultant/pharmacy verification.

action.message: Permanently discontinue both medicines for Grade 4 cutaneous reactions.

rules.explanation: Permanently discontinue both medicines for Grade 4 cutaneous reactions.

action.message: Confirm peak grade and recurrence. First Grade 2/3 may restart at the same dose; recurrent Grade 2 reduces binimetinib only, recurrent Grade 3 reduces both. Prior Grade 4 remains a permanent-stop pathway.

rules.explanation: Confirm peak grade and recurrence. First Grade 2/3 may restart at the same dose; recurrent Grade 2 reduces binimetinib only, recurrent Grade 3 reduces both. Prior Grade 4 remains a permanent-stop pathway.

action.message: Hold binimetinib for up to 2 weeks, arrange ophthalmology including OCT as appropriate, and repeat visual acuity assessment.

rules.explanation: Hold binimetinib for up to 2 weeks, arrange ophthalmology including OCT as appropriate, and repeat visual acuity assessment.

action.message: While binimetinib is interrupted, the source reduces encorafenib from 450 to 300 mg daily. Confirm actual dose and prior reductions; never automatically increase an already lower dose. Permanent binimetinib discontinuation also discontinues encorafenib.

rules.explanation: While binimetinib is interrupted, the source reduces encorafenib from 450 to 300 mg daily. Confirm actual dose and prior reductions; never automatically increase an already lower dose. Permanent binimetinib discontinuation also discontinues encorafenib.

action.message: Symptomatic Grade 4 RPED with Grade 4 visual acuity loss requires permanent binimetinib discontinuation. Permanently stopping binimetinib also requires encorafenib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Symptomatic Grade 4 RPED with Grade 4 visual acuity loss requires permanent binimetinib discontinuation. Permanently stopping binimetinib also requires encorafenib discontinuation.

action.message: Confirmed RVO requires permanent binimetinib discontinuation. Permanently stopping binimetinib also requires encorafenib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Confirmed RVO requires permanent binimetinib discontinuation. Permanently stopping binimetinib also requires encorafenib discontinuation.

action.message: After the RPED hold of up to 2 weeks: Grade 0–1 permits same-dose restart; improvement only to Grade 2 permits a lower dose; failure to improve to Grade 2 requires permanent binimetinib discontinuation and linked encorafenib discontinuation. Confirm ophthalmic findings and actual timing/doses.

rules.explanation: After the RPED hold of up to 2 weeks: Grade 0–1 permits same-dose restart; improvement only to Grade 2 permits a lower dose; failure to improve to Grade 2 requires permanent binimetinib discontinuation and linked encorafenib discontinuation. Confirm ophthalmic findings and actual timing/doses.

action.message: RPED has not improved to Grade 2 after the 2-week hold; permanently discontinue binimetinib. Permanently stopping binimetinib also requires encorafenib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: RPED has not improved to Grade 2 after the 2-week hold; permanently discontinue binimetinib. Permanently stopping binimetinib also requires encorafenib discontinuation.

action.message: Confirm RPED symptoms and visual-acuity grade. Do not substitute a generic ocular hold/stop for the exact source classification.

rules.explanation: Confirm RPED symptoms and visual-acuity grade. Do not substitute a generic ocular hold/stop for the exact source classification.

action.message: Hold encorafenib for Grade 3 uveitis or Grade 1–2 refractory to local therapy; repeat ophthalmic assessment within 2 weeks. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

rules.explanation: Hold encorafenib for Grade 3 uveitis or Grade 1–2 refractory to local therapy; repeat ophthalmic assessment within 2 weeks. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

action.message: Grade 4 uveitis requires permanent encorafenib discontinuation and ophthalmic follow-up. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 uveitis requires permanent encorafenib discontinuation and ophthalmic follow-up. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

action.message: Persistent uveitis without required improvement within 6 weeks requires permanent encorafenib discontinuation and repeat ophthalmic monitoring. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

rules.explanation: Persistent uveitis without required improvement within 6 weeks requires permanent encorafenib discontinuation and repeat ophthalmic monitoring. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

action.message: Previous Grade 1 must improve to Grade 0 for same-dose encorafenib restart; previous Grade 2–3 must improve to Grade 0–1 for reduced-dose restart. Failure within 6 weeks or Grade 4 follows permanent-stop rules. Confirm current grade and component doses.

rules.explanation: Previous Grade 1 must improve to Grade 0 for same-dose encorafenib restart; previous Grade 2–3 must improve to Grade 0–1 for reduced-dose restart. Failure within 6 weeks or Grade 4 follows permanent-stop rules. Confirm current grade and component doses.

action.message: Confirm response to local ocular treatment before choosing the Grade 1–2 uveitis pathway.

rules.explanation: Confirm response to local ocular treatment before choosing the Grade 1–2 uveitis pathway.

action.message: Hold binimetinib for up to 4 weeks for Grade 2 LVEF decrease or absolute fall >10 points with LVEF below LLN; assess LVEF every 2 weeks and determine symptoms.

rules.explanation: Hold binimetinib for up to 4 weeks for Grade 2 LVEF decrease or absolute fall >10 points with LVEF below LLN; assess LVEF every 2 weeks and determine symptoms.

action.message: While binimetinib is interrupted, the source reduces encorafenib from 450 to 300 mg daily. Confirm actual dose and prior reductions; never automatically increase an already lower dose. Permanent binimetinib discontinuation also discontinues encorafenib.

rules.explanation: While binimetinib is interrupted, the source reduces encorafenib from 450 to 300 mg daily. Confirm actual dose and prior reductions; never automatically increase an already lower dose. Permanent binimetinib discontinuation also discontinues encorafenib.

action.message: Grade 3–4 LVEF decrease or symptomatic LVD requires permanent binimetinib discontinuation; evaluate LVEF every 2 weeks until recovery. Permanently stopping binimetinib also requires encorafenib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Grade 3–4 LVEF decrease or symptomatic LVD requires permanent binimetinib discontinuation; evaluate LVEF every 2 weeks until recovery. Permanently stopping binimetinib also requires encorafenib discontinuation.

action.message: LVEF failed to recover within 4 weeks to both at/above LLN AND no more than 10 points below baseline; permanently discontinue binimetinib. Permanently stopping binimetinib also requires encorafenib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: LVEF failed to recover within 4 weeks to both at/above LLN AND no more than 10 points below baseline; permanently discontinue binimetinib. Permanently stopping binimetinib also requires encorafenib discontinuation.

action.message: Both cardiac recovery criteria are met within 4 weeks. Consider reduced-dose binimetinib after consultant review; do not re-escalate a dose reduced for LVD.

rules.explanation: Both cardiac recovery criteria are met within 4 weeks. Consider reduced-dose binimetinib after consultant review; do not re-escalate a dose reduced for LVD.

action.message: QTcF >500 ms with increase ≤60 ms: hold encorafenib; reduced-dose restart only when QTcF ≤500 ms. More than one recurrence requires discontinuation. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

rules.explanation: QTcF >500 ms with increase ≤60 ms: hold encorafenib; reduced-dose restart only when QTcF ≤500 ms. More than one recurrence requires discontinuation. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

action.message: QTcF >500 ms AND increase >60 ms from pretreatment requires permanent encorafenib discontinuation. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

rules.explanation: QTcF >500 ms AND increase >60 ms from pretreatment requires permanent encorafenib discontinuation. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

action.message: QTcF exceeds 500 ms but the pretreatment value is missing. Hold and obtain baseline/recurrence information; do not infer the ≤60-ms pathway. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

rules.explanation: QTcF exceeds 500 ms but the pretreatment value is missing. Hold and obtain baseline/recurrence information; do not infer the ≤60-ms pathway. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

action.message: More than one QTcF recurrence requires encorafenib discontinuation even if the current QTcF has recovered. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

rules.explanation: More than one QTcF recurrence requires encorafenib discontinuation even if the current QTcF has recovered. If encorafenib is held, also hold binimetinib; permanent encorafenib discontinuation also discontinues binimetinib.

action.message: QTcF recovery to ≤500 ms is only one restart requirement. Confirm peak QTcF increase, recurrence count, electrolyte correction and prior dose; a prior >60-ms rise with QTcF >500 or >1 recurrence remains a stop pathway.

rules.explanation: QTcF recovery to ≤500 ms is only one restart requirement. Confirm peak QTcF increase, recurrence count, electrolyte correction and prior dose; a prior >60-ms rise with QTcF >500 or >1 recurrence remains a stop pathway.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Current NCCP 00563 v4 p8: both components moderate-to-high; follow local oral antiemetic policy.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
other_supportive_care: Use locally prescribed antiemetics and symptom support; no universal prophylactic medicine doses are stated.
Adequate fluid intake and clinician-directed CK/renal monitoring; consider prophylactic hydration for tumour lysis risk.
Effective contraception during treatment and at least 1 month after the last dose. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may fall: use an additional or alternative effective method as directed.
Discuss potential impaired spermatogenesis, fertility preservation and fetal harm risk.

baseline: Dermatologic evaluation for other skin cancer
during: FBC, renal and liver profile monthly
CK and creatinine monthly for the first 6 months, then as clinically indicated
ECG at initiation, after 4 weeks, then every 12 weeks and after dose modification
LVEF by echocardiogram/MUGA every 3 months or more often as indicated
Blood pressure during treatment; visual symptom review at each visit
Dermatology every 60 days; head/neck every 3 months; chest CT every 6 months
Closer monitoring for mild hepatic impairment and tumour lysis risk; additional tests follow symptoms and the clinical plan
after: Dermatology for up to 6 months after discontinuation; other surveillance follows the consultant plan
monitoring.disease_monitoring: Individual consultant plan; source surveillance CT is not an automatic tumour-response scan schedule or a universal tumour-marker panel.
